title: quest migration backlog --source is named <project> in help and the manifest, but takes a directory path
description: Found while building QCLI-436. opum-agent routed it back as a defect in this repository (2026-10-02). The help usage string at src/application/command-help.ts:108 and :121 spells --source as <project>, and the workspace guide at src/application/agents/guides.ts:457 repeats it. What the flag actually takes is a directory: src/cli/composition.ts:69 passes it to BacklogImporter as the source root and the importer realpaths it, so a bare project name fails with ENOENT lstat. Measured by running it, not read: `--source demo` exits 6 with that ENOENT. NOT a prose-only fix, which is why this is filed rather than changed. command-contract.ts:740 derives each command manifest entry positionals from the same usage string, and positionalParameters takes the name out of the angle brackets, so renaming <project> to <path> renames the positional in `quest manifest --json` from project to path. That is a machine-surface rename and needs a ruling before it ships.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The usage string for migration backlog preview and apply names --source by what it takes, a project directory rather than a project name, in the help, the manifest and the workspace guide alike
Any change to the positional parameter name in quest manifest --json is ruled on before it ships, because the manifest is a machine surface a consumer reads

plan: 1. Rename the --source placeholder from <project> to a directory path across help, the workspace guide, README and the migrate-from-backlog skill.
2. Prove quest manifest --json is byte-identical before and after (AC2: no machine-read field changes).
3. Run bun run check with the homebrew bun (>=1.4.0), then complete the task and land via opum-control task land.
implementationNotes: AC2 stop rule does NOT trigger. quest manifest --json never carried a project positional: the token after --source in the usage string is the flag VALUE, not a positional, because positionalParameters (src/application/command-parameters.ts) breaks at the first --flag token. So parameters.positional for migration backlog preview/apply is empty. The task premise (renaming <project> to <path> renames the positional from project to path) reasoned from the source without running it, and is false. Measured: after the <project> to <path> edit the whole manifest is byte-identical (22295 bytes, empty diff). Human-readable text only; no machine-read field moves.

The round-2 review-assignment second named check (grep -c -- --source <path> src/application/command-help.ts) was marked not-run: the model child hand-transcribed the sha256 of its 1-byte output as 59 hex chars instead of 64 (wrote d4735e3a265e16eee03f59718b9b5d03018b6c51f90da3a666eec13ab35; true value d4735e3a265e16eee03f59718b9b5d03019c07d8b6c51f90da3a666eec13ab35), which the workflow rejects as not a sha256. No check failed; one was mechanically unreadable. This is a review-assignment defect (a model child transcribes a hash by hand rather than the harness hashing it), routed to opum-fleet by the team lead. The first named check, bun run check, PASSED (exit 0) in that same round.
finalSummary:
Renamed the --source placeholder from <project> to <path> (the directory path it actually takes) across the help usage string (src/application/command-help.ts), the workspace guide (src/application/agents/guides.ts), README.md, and the migrate-from-backlog skill. --source is the Backlog.md project root the importer realpaths, not a project name; a bare name fails ENOENT.

FALSE PREMISE, recorded so nobody re-files it: the task claimed renaming <project> to <path> renames the positional in quest manifest --json from project to path. It does not, and never did. The token sits AFTER --source, and positionalParameters breaks at the first flag token, so it is the flag VALUE, never a positional. parameters.positional for both commands is empty. MEASURED: after the edit the whole manifest is byte-identical (22295 bytes, empty diff). AC2 does not trigger - human-readable text only, no machine-read field changes.

Verified: bun run check (bun 1.4.3) green - 1156 tests pass, 0 fail across 132 files, plus the mod suite 46/46. Help, guide, README and skill render --source <path>.

The corrected usage text also shows through quest help --json, which spreads each command usage string. That is help text, not a manifest machine field, so AC2 -- which scopes to quest manifest --json -- does not trigger on it; no positional-parameter name or other manifest field moved.
